The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V. Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A. No. 2452 of 2015
 And
 M.A.C.M.A. No. 2474 of 2015
Common Judgment

:
-
1) Aggrieved by the impugned Decree and Order, dated 17.07.2015, passed in M.V.O.P. No. 370 of 2013 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Principal District Judge,
Kadapa, whereby, the claim of Rs.12,04,371.47 paise was awarded to the claimant No.2 towards compensation, M.A.C.M.A. No. 2474 of 2015 is filed by the claimants for claiming remaining balance compensation amount and M.A.C.M.A. 2452 of 2015 is filed by the sole respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C., questioning the legal validity of the Order passed by the Tribunal.

Since,
both these appeals are filed against one Order and Decree, dated 17.07.2015, passed by the Tribunal in M.V.O.P. No.370 of 2013, both these appeals are heard together and disposed of by way of Common Judgment.
2) For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the Appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3) Originally, the claim petition was filed by the 1st claimant [Sri. Thirupathigari Pramod Kumar - the 'deceased'] under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [the 'M.V. Act'], and Rule 476 of A.P. Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 [the 'Rules'] against the respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C., claiming compensation of Rs.22,40,500/- for a motor vehicle accident that took place on 27.09.2012 and upon his death, his father in the capacity as 'legal representative' came on record as "2nd claimant".

4) Facts germane to dispose of the Appeal may briefly be stated as follows: -
i. On 27.09.2012 at about 4.20 P.M., the 1st claimant met with an accident near Seetharamapuram cross road on Porumamilla - Badvel main road, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.AP28 Z 638 and he was admitted in the hospital and while undergoing treatment he died on 29.12.2013 on account of injuries sustained by him in the accident that took place on 27.09.2012.

The Porumamilla Police registered a case in crime No. 169 of 2012 against the driver of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C.
bus.

5) The sole respondent filed counter with a plea that the respondent is not liable to Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... vs Thirupathigari Pramod Kumar Another on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149816258/
1 pay any compensation and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the deceased.
6) Based on the above pleadings, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
(i) Whether the accident took place on 27.09.2012 at about 4.20 P.M. near Seetharamapuram cross road on Porumamilla to Badvel main road due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing No. AP28 Z 638 resulting in death of the deceased by name T. Pramod Kumar?
(ii) Whether the claimant No. 2 is entitled to claim compensation, if so to what extent, and from which of the respondents?

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(iii) To what relief?
7)
During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioners, PW1 to PW6 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A12 and Ex.X1 and Ex.X2 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent, no witnesses were examined and no documents are marked.

8) At the culmination of the enquiry and on appreciation of the entire evidence available on record, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.12,04,371.47 paise towards total compensation to the claimant No.2.
Aggrieved thereby, the claimants and the sole respondent preferred the aforesaid appeals separately.

9) Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
10) Now, the point for determination is:
i) Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?
If so, to what extent?
ii) Whether the appellants/claimants are entitled to remaining balance compensation amount, as prayed in the claim application?

11) POINT Nos. (i) & (ii): As seen from the material on record, the claimant No. 1 met with an accident on 27.09.2012 at 4.20 P.M. near Seetharamapuram cross road on Porumamilla - Badvel main road, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.AP28 Z 638 and died on 29.12.2013 on account of injuries sustained by him, in the accident that took place, on 27.09.2012.
12) The 2nd claimant/father of the deceased/1st claimant came on record claiming himself as a legal representative of the deceased/1st claimant and as a dependent.

Since during the pendency of the Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... vs Thirupathigari Pramod Kumar Another on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149816258/
2 claim application, the 1st claimant/injured [Pramod Kumar] died, his father came on record as 2nd claimant.

sentences.text: On considering the entire material on record and on considering Ex.A1 - certified copy of the F.I.R., Ex.A3 - certified copy of the charge-sheet and Ex.A2 - certified copy of the wound certificate so also the evidence of PW3, who was an eye witness to the accident and the rider of the motorcycle, on which the injured [Pramod Kumar] was proceeding, the Tribunal rightly arrived at a conclusion that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.AP28 Z 638, as a result, the deceased sustained injuries.

In-fact, the material on record supports that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No. AP28 Z 638, in which the injured [Pramod Kumar]
received serious injuries and he was also bedridden for a prolonged period.

13) Coming to the compensation, the Tribunal by assailing reasons came to conclusion that the 2nd claimant failed to prove that his son i.e., 1st claimant died due to the injuries sustained in the accident in question.

The material on record reveals that the injured/1st claimant was admitted in the Government Hospital, Porumamilla, and from there he was shifted to Himalaya Multi Speciality Hospital and later he was shifted to Apollo Hospital, Chennai and, thereafter, he was shifted to S.V.R.R. Hospital, Tirupathi, and got discharged from the said hospital.

The material on record further reveals that, since the 1st claimant was unable to attend natural calls, certain pipes were arranged for passing of urine and stools and one Siva Reddy [Physiotherapist] was engaged to do physiotherapy to the 1st claimant by spending huge amount and the 2nd claimant also spent more money for supplying nutritious food to the 1st claimant.

14) On considering the evidence of PW4 to PW6 and on considering Ex.A6, the Tribunal arrived at a conclusion that PW1 spent a total sum of Rs.11,31,611.47 paise, which is supported by Ex.A6 final bill.
Therefore, the said amount is awarded to the 2nd claimant towards medical expenses in addition to the amount spent under Ex.A8 - medical bill of Rs.2,760/-.
In total, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.11,34,371.47 paise.

15) As stated supra, the material on record clearly reveals that as the injured was unable to attend natural calls, certain pipes were arranged for passing of urine and stools and he was bedridden for long time.
A physiotherapist was also engaged by the 2nd claimant.
Therefore, the said amount awarded by the Tribunal is quite reasonable amount.
There is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

16) The Tribunal by giving reasons held that, "in view of the nature of injuries sustained by the injured, the 2nd claimant engaged a four-wheeler for transportation of injured from Porumamilla to Chennai and from Chennai to Tirupathi and from Tirupathi to Porumamilla.

By assailing reasons,
the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.20,000/- under the head of 'transport expenses'.
On considering the nature of injuries sustained by the 1st claimant, I am of the considered view that, it is desirable to award further amount of Rs.20,000/- under the head of 'transport expenses'.

Therefore, in total, the 2nd claimant is entitled to an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards 'transport expenses', since the injured was travelled from Porumamilla to Chennai and from Chennai to Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... vs Thirupathigari Pramod Kumar

3 Tirupathi and from Tirupathi to Porumamilla by engaging four-wheeler car by the 2nd claimant/father of the injured.

17) As stated supra, the injured also sustained head injury and he was unconscious and unable to speak and lost memory and as he was unable to attend natural calls, certain pipes were arranged for passing urine and stools.
Certainly, the injured had to be travelled in a four-wheeler car to go to hospitals to reach far away places.

Therefore, it is desirable to award an amount of Rs.40,000/-
under the head of 'transport expenses'.
18)
As stated supra, the 2nd claimant engaged one S.A. Sikur to attend on the 1st claimant on payment of monthly salary of Rs.4,000/-.
In order to prove the same, the 2 nd claimant examined S.A. Sikur as 'PW2'.
As per his evidence, he received Rs.44,000/- towards wages for eleven months besides travelling charges per day Rs.20/-.
Therefore, on considering the entire evidence on record and entire material available on record, an amount of Rs.44,000/- was awarded under the head of 'attendant charges'.
As stated supra, the injured was treated in Government Hospital, Porumamilla,
initially, from there, he was shifted to Himalaya Multi Speciality Hospital, Kadapa, and from there he was shifted to Apollo Hospital, Chennai.
As stated supra, the injured was unconscious and unable to speak and lost memory and he was unable to attend to natural calls.

Therefore, it is desirable to award an amount of Rs.30,000/- towards extra-nourishment on food in-stead of Rs.20,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

19) In the result, the appeal filed by the A.P. State Road Transport Corporation vide M.A.C.M.A. No.
2452 of 2015 is dismissed and the appeal filed by the claimants vide M.A.C.M.A. No. 2474 of 2015 is partly allowed.
The claim of Rs.12,04,371/- awarded by Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.12,38,371/-.
The claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.34,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim application till the date of realization.
The respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C. is directed to deposit the said enhanced compensation of Rs.34,000/- with interest at 7.5% per annum, as ordered above, within two months from the date of this judgment.
On such deposit, the 2nd claimant is entitled to withdraw the same along with interest therein.
The impugned Order in M.V.O.P. No. 370 of 2013 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Kadapa, is modified to the extent as stated above.

20) As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Appeal shall stand closed.
